title: Telco customer churn (11.1.3+)
venue: IBM Community: Cognos Analytics blog (Base Samples); mirrored on Kaggle by user BlastChar as 'Telco Customer Churn'
harvard_reference:
IBM (2019) 'Telco customer churn (11.1.3+)', IBM Community: Cognos Analytics blog, 11 July. Available at: https://community.ibm.com/community/user/blogs/steven-macko/2019/07/11/telco-customer-churn-1113 (Accessed: 27 September 2026).
BlastChar (no date) Telco Customer Churn [Dataset]. Kaggle. Available at: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/blastchar/telco-customer-churn (Accessed: 27 September 2026).
abstract_summary: Not a paper, so there is no abstract. The IBM Community post (by 'Samples Team', posted 11 July 2019, filed under the Cognos Analytics blog at the URL slug steven-macko) announces that, in IBM Cognos Analytics 11.1.3, the 'Telco Customer Churn' data module in the Base Samples was enhanced 'to provide a wider narrative'. Its description reads, verbatim: 'The Telco customer churn data contains information about a fictional telco company that provided home phone and Internet services to 7043 customers in California in Q3. It indicates which customers have left, stayed, or signed up for their service. Multiple important demographics are included for each customer, as well as a Satisfaction Score, Churn Score, and Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) index.' The enhanced data module is composed of five uploaded files/tables (Demographics, Location, Population, Services, Status) and the post documents every field: the Status table includes Satisfaction Score, Customer Status (Churned/Stayed/Joined at the end of the quarter), Churn Label, Churn Value, Churn Score (0-100, from IBM SPSS Modeler), Churn Score Category, CLTV, CLTV Category, Churn Category and Churn Reason; the Services table adds fields absent from the Kaggle file (Offer, Referred a Friend, Number of Referrals, Avg Monthly Long Distance Charges, Avg Monthly GB Download, Streaming Music, Unlimited Data, Total Refunds, Total Extra Data Charges, Total Long Distance Charges). Four 'interesting scenarios' illustrate the narrative (e.g. churn clustered in San Diego-area zip codes with reason 'Competitor made better offer'; low satisfaction scores among churners; month-to-month contracts associated with churn). The Kaggle mirror (owner BlastChar, subtitle 'Focused customer retention programs', Version 1, one file WA_Fn-UseC_-Telco-Customer-Churn.csv, 977.5 kB) quotes '[IBM Sample Data Sets]' in its Context, states 'The raw data contains 7043 rows (customers) and 21 columns (features)', explains that the Churn column captures 'Customers who left within the last month', lists the service/account/demographic attribute groups, and links to the IBM Community post as the 'New version from IBM'.

claims_supported.claim: The data describe a fictional telco that provided home phone and internet services to 7,043 customers in California in Q3, and indicate which customers left, stayed or signed up within the last month.
claims_supported.where: PARTIAL ONLY (minor wording conflation). The first clause is supported verbatim by the IBM Community post's opening description: 'a fictional telco company that provided home phone and Internet services to 7043 customers in California in Q3. It indicates which customers have left, stayed, or signed up for their service.' However, the source never says customers 'stayed or signed up within the last month'. The phrase 'within the last month' appears in the post only in relation to the churn column ('The churn column indicates whether or not the customer left within the last month' in the data-module description, and the same wording for the Churn Label column in the 'Telco churn' dashboard and exploration descriptions), and the Kaggle page likewise says 'Customers who left within the last month - the column is called Churn'. Moreover, the post's own field dictionary defines the window as a quarter, not a month: 'Customer Status: Indicates the status of the customer at the end of the quarter: Churned, Stayed, or Joined' and 'Churn Label: Yes = the customer left the company this quarter'. Suggested fix: 'The data describe a fictional telco that provided home phone and internet services to 7,043 customers in California in Q3 and indicate which customers left, stayed or signed up for the service (IBM, 2019); in the Kaggle release the target column, Churn, flags customers who left within the last month (BlastChar, no date).' Written that way the claim is fully supported.

claims_supported.claim: The Kaggle version (blastchar) has 7,043 rows and 21 columns and no Churn Score / Churn Reason / CLTV columns, unlike IBM's extended version.
claims_supported.where: Kaggle page (kaggle.com/datasets/blastchar/telco-customer-churn), 'About this file' panel: 'The raw data contains 7043 rows (customers) and 21 columns (features). The "Churn" column is our target.'; the Data Explorer sidebar shows '1 file', '21 columns' and the column viewer shows '10 of 21 columns' with customerID reported as 7043 unique values. The absence of Churn Score, Churn Reason and CLTV is a negative claim, verified by enumerating the 21 columns: the Kaggle page names customerID, gender, SeniorCitizen, Partner, Dependents, tenure, PhoneService, MultipleLines, InternetService, OnlineSecurity (first 10) and its Content section lists the remaining attribute groups (online backup, device protection, tech support, streaming TV and movies, contract, payment method, paperless billing, monthly charges, total charges, Churn); the header of the identical WA_Fn-UseC_ file mirrored in IBM's own GitHub repository (IBM/telco-customer-churn-on-icp4d, data/Telco-Customer-Churn.csv) was read and contains exactly 21 fields: customerID, gender, SeniorCitizen, Partner, Dependents, tenure, PhoneService, MultipleLines, InternetService, OnlineSecurity, OnlineBackup, DeviceProtection, TechSupport, StreamingTV, StreamingMovies, Contract, PaperlessBilling, PaymentMethod, MonthlyCharges, TotalCharges, Churn - none of Churn Score, Churn Reason, CLTV, Satisfaction Score, Churn Label or Churn Value. The 'unlike IBM's extended version' part is supported by the IBM Community post's Status table, which documents Churn Score ('A value from 0-100 that is calculated using the predictive tool IBM SPSS Modeler'), Churn Reason ('A customer's specific reason for leaving the company') and CLTV ('Customer Lifetime Value. A predicted CLTV is calculated using corporate formulas and existing data'), together with Satisfaction Score, Churn Category and many extra Services fields. Note: the exact row count 7,043 was not independently recounted from the file (no download was made); it rests on the Kaggle page's own statement and the IBM description of 7043 customers.

verification_notes: This is a sample data set / web resource, not a journal article, so Crossref and Semantic Scholar are not applicable and no DOI exists for either the IBM post or the Kaggle mirror (the Kaggle 'DOI Citation' metadata field is empty, '-'). IBM page verified directly in the built-in browser: title 'Telco customer churn (11.1.3+)', byline 'By Samples Team posted 07/11/19 08:15 AM' (US date format, i.e. 11 July 2019, matching the /2019/07/11/ path), filed in the Cognos Analytics community blog; the lead's URL (…/community/user/businessanalytics/blogs/steven-macko/2019/07/11/telco-customer-churn-1113) resolves and redirects to the permalink …/community/user/blogs/steven-macko/2019/07/11/telco-customer-churn-1113, which is the URL used in the reference (either works). The 'steven-macko' slug is an account path; the displayed author is 'Samples Team', so a corporate author (IBM) is used, consistent with the Kaggle page's attribution to 'IBM Sample Data Sets'. Full text of the post was read, including the five-table field dictionary quoted in the claim checks. Kaggle page verified in the built-in browser (plain HTTP fetches of kaggle.com returned a reCAPTCHA interstitial, which was not bypassed; the browser rendered the public page normally): owner BlastChar, title 'Telco Customer Churn', subtitle 'Focused customer retention programs', 'Updated 9 years ago', Version 1, single file WA_Fn-UseC_-Telco-Customer-Churn.csv (977.5 kB), 21 columns, '7043 rows (customers) and 21 columns (features)', licence 'Data files (c) Original Authors', usability 8.82, Context quoting '[IBM Sample Data Sets]', and the 'New version from IBM' link to the IBM Community post. Kaggle metadata sections (Authors, Coverage, DOI Citation, Provenance sources/citations) are all empty. The Kaggle page displays only a relative date ('9 years ago' as of 27 September 2026, i.e. roughly 2017 to early 2018); no absolute upload date is exposed on the dataset page, the hover tooltip or the /versions/1 view, so the year for the mirror is left unverified and the mirror reference uses '(no date)'. Many published papers cite it as 'BlastChar (2018)', which is consistent with the relative date but was not confirmed here. The 21-column header was corroborated from IBM's own GitHub mirror of the same CSV (raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/telco-customer-churn-on-icp4d/master/data/Telco-Customer-Churn.csv) without downloading the file; row count was not recounted. The IBM docs pages (ibm.com/docs, Cognos Analytics 11.1.x 'Telco churn relationships exploration sample' and 12.1.x 'Telco customer churn') were also fetched and use the same 'fictional telco company' / 'left within the last month' wording but do not restate the 7043/California/Q3 sentence. A search snippet claiming the IBM version has '33 variables' was not verified on any IBM page and is not relied on (the 11.1.3+ module is split across five tables, so a single column count is not meaningful).
caveats: (1) The IBM post is internally inconsistent about the churn window: the narrative text says the churn column flags customers who 'left within the last month', while the field dictionary defines Churn Label/Customer Status per fiscal quarter ('left the company this quarter'; 'status … at the end of the quarter: Churned, Stayed, or Joined'). The report should not assert a precise churn window as fact; the safest phrasing is 'customers who left within the last month (as described on Kaggle)' or 'who churned during the quarter (per IBM's field definitions)'. (2) The Kaggle file is the older 21-column WA_Fn-UseC_ release of IBM Watson Analytics sample data; it is not a subset of the 11.1.3+ five-table module in any documented one-to-one sense (field names differ, e.g. 'tenure' vs 'Tenure in Months', 'PaymentMethod' values differ), so the report should describe the IBM post as documenting the enhanced version rather than as the source of the Kaggle CSV's exact schema. (3) Neither resource has a DOI or a named individual author; cite IBM as corporate author and BlastChar as the Kaggle uploader, each with an accessed date. (4) The Kaggle upload date could not be verified (relative date only); if the report needs a year for the mirror, '2018' is plausible but should be checked against the Kaggle metadata API or the version history when logged in, otherwise use '(no date)'. (5) The 7,043-row figure is taken from the pages' own statements, not from an independent recount. (6) Kaggle's licence is 'Data files (c) Original Authors' (i.e. IBM), which the report's data-ethics section may need to acknowledge.
